question_text:
The following true stresses produce the corresponding true plastic strains for a brass alloy:

| True Stress (psi) | True Strain |
| :--: | :--: |
| 60,000 | 0.15 |
| 70,000 | 0.25 |

What true stress is necessary to produce a true plastic strain of 0.21 ?The unit of the answer is MPa.
response:
Using the Hollomon equation $\sigma = K\varepsilon^n$:

$$n = \frac{\ln(\sigma_2/\sigma_1)}{\ln(\varepsilon_2/\varepsilon_1)} = \frac{\ln(70000/60000)}{\ln(0.25/0.15)} \approx 0.3018$$

$$K = \sigma_1/\varepsilon_1^n \approx 106360 \text{ psi}$$

$$\sigma = K(0.21)^n \approx 66412 \text{ psi} \approx 457.9 \text{ MPa}$$

$$\boxed{457.9}$$
